utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We continue with the evidence of Mr. Djordjevic today. I won't bother to remind you each day, Mr. Djordjevic, but the affirmation you made at the beginning applies throughout your evidence. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. However, before we proceed, I would like to say something. We have received a document with a translation, so I would like to thank the translation service for being so expeditious. It was a document that was marked for identification as D397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be now received as an exhibit, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, now I would like to ask you to move on to document number 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit P257 called up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision made by the minister of the interior, Vlajko Stojiljkovic. It was passed on the 18th of June, 1998. It has to do with the establishment of the 124th Intervention Brigade of the PJP. On the basis of the authority vested in him on the basis of Article 6 of the Law on the Interior, the minister made this decision and established the 124th Intervention Brigade. Its tasks are spelled out here. First of all, how it was made up initially, the intervention brigade, and then also what its tasks and duties are. Also how it is put on the ready, also how they are professionally trained, how the brigade is manned, and on page 2 of the same document we see how and in which way the members of this brigade are going to be listed in lists of establishment. And there is the obligation to compile a document on the establishment of this brigade that is supposed to contain attachments on various bases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please tell us now who made decisions about the engagement of the PJP units in Kosovo, to have them sent in Kosovo in the first place?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this decision and in regulations in general, the only authorised person to order the assembling and engagement of the PJPs was the minister of the interior or an official authorised by him. That is what regulations say. Although I, as chief of the RJB, never received any authority from him to use any PJP or part of any PJP to be sent out on any mission whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there a difference in procedure when PJPs are being sent to Kosova-Metohija or on any other security mission?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure was absolutely the same. After the minister would make his decision, the service, or rather, the administration in charge in the Ministry of the Interior would write up a dispatch ordering the secretariats which part of the unit they would send to which area and using which vehicles, how they will be dressed and so on. That was the principle involved. So regardless of what their mission would be it was the obligation of that administration only to provide a route for their movement and to tell them who they are supposed to report to over there and how they are supposed to be equipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who does the planning? Who issues tasks to the units that were sent to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday we talked about the obligations of these units and who gives them their assignments, and we talked about situations, say, in Belgrade, when law and order are being disturbed in any way. The units report to where they had been dispatched, and these units carry out tasks in accordance with plans of those staffs or secretariats, if I can put it that way, where they had been sent. So their tasks are planned, and that institution where they had been sent gives them orders as to what to do. If it's a secretariat, that is a secretariat where they had been sent or where they were attached. And if they are being put at the disposal of a staff, then their tasks are going to be planned by a staff. And the staff will issue all orders in relation to the discharge of the tasks on the basis of these plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P132.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your binder it is document 35. Mr. Djordjevic, it is your dispatch dated the 19th of June 1998, and could you please give us your comments in respect of this dispatch that you had sent.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent this dispatch on the 19th of June 1998, that is to say after the minister's decision had been made. Actually, this is not a dispatch, it's a letter. So this is my letter sent to all Secretariats of the Interior and enclosed is the minister's decision. Basically this letter of mine informs the Secretariats of the Interior from the areas -- the area of Kosova-Metohija whose members actually made up this brigade. I informed them that the minister had made his decision, and I provide some kind of instructions about equal treatment on the part of all secretariats when carrying out this decision. The entire documentation of this 124th Intervention Brigade should be compiled in the same way in all secretariats. So practically this is an instruction that I'm giving them and in this way I provide some detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You corrected me, and you said that this was a letter. Who created the letter within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All documents in relation to PJPs and all logistical work in relation to these units in the Ministry of Interior were carried out by the police administration. Thereby, it was the police administration that had written up this letter too. They gave it to me to sign. They attached the minister's decision to it, and distributed this document to the secretariats that it pertained to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now please have Defence Exhibit D001-2948. For my colleagues from the Prosecution, it is 1453. That's the 65 ter number from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, for you it is number 34. Actually, you've already told us that in accordance with Article 6, the minister could make decisions on the establishment of PJPs. I'm referring to the rules on internal organisation. So could you please tell us in respect of this decision how things functioned in practice? I mean, in terms of these special anti-terrorist units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was based on the same authority given to him by law, and it was passed on the 5th of April 1996 by minister Zoran Sokolovic. You can see that on page 2 of this decision. In principle, this decision, just like the previous one, contains the same obligations. The first obligation is the minister's decision to establish a Special Anti-terrorist Unit as a separate police unit, as a separate unit within the RJB. Its headquarters are in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina. So just something by way of clarification here, this decision establishes that there is a Special Anti-terrorist Unit in the following form: One unit with three headquarters, Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina. Up until then in the RJB, there had been three special units, and they were attached to the secretariats in Novi Sad, the Novi Sad secretariat, in Novi Sad, and then in Pristina attached to the Pristina secretariat, and in Belgrade, there was one that was organisationally linked to the police administration at the headquarters of the secretariat. This decision, this document means that the minister pools these three units and places them under one command. That is the command of the Special Anti-terrorist Unit. Further on their tasks are spelled out in this decision, how personnel will be deployed, and on page 2 of this decision, you can see that all previous decisions are declared null and void, those that regulated the activity of the special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please tell us who made decisions on sending the Special Anti-terrorist Unit out on mission or part of the unit?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like in the case of the PJPs, it was the minister who had the authority to send the Special Anti-terrorist Unit out on a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us about equipment and training of the anti-terrorist unit. How was that carried out? Who did that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The anti-terrorist unit, established in this way, had within its command persons who were involved in training. First of all, they had to compile programmes of training drawing on worldwide and European experience. Such a plan was approved by the officers in charge, and they carried out this training according to such plans for various situations for the purposes of which this unit had been established. It has to be noted that this involved the air force too and also different hostage situations, persons that had been barricaded, fighting terrorist groups, and so on and so forth. So all obligations that this unit had had to be studied in detail on the basis of the programme adopted. They were supposed to train on that basis too, and to be ready to act. As a rule, they were used for the most complex security-related tasks. That is to say when another unit from the ministry could not do this most complex work, then it would be the Special Anti-terrorist Unit that would be engaged. In this relation, there were special criteria for equipping the Special Anti-terrorist Unit. They had special uniforms and also the other weapons they required and other equipment they required. With regard to this work and with regard to their equipment, they also had logistical support from the police administration, and as for their experience with the PJPs, that only contributed to the overall preparations for the Special Anti-terrorist Unit, and for making them more successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who planned and who issued assignments to the whole unit, or a part of a unit that was engaged in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this unit as well as other attached and resubordinated units, all the assignments and orders were given by the staff of the ministry. And those who executed them directly on the ground were unit commanders and their command staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us about any activities that were executed. Who did the unit commanders report to thereafter in Kosovo and Metohija, I mean?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit, like all attached units, had to report to the authority who issued them with the assignment, depending on the territory. They would report to the staff that had given them the assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify a little. You said that this unit had bases in three places, what was the strength of these units, and perhaps if you know the composition, how much of the personnel was actually operations personnel?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The strength of these units according to the rules was 80 men per unit, that would mean 200 or 250 men in total. But a large number of men within units were involved in logistical and other non-operative tasks. Each of these three anti-terrorist units worked in groups or squads, and I believe each of the groups had three to four units numbering ten men each. So if you look at the total of the members of these anti-terrorist units, half of them approximately were engaged in operations tasks and the rest were dealing with the logistics and other work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: With this kind of strength and distribution across centres in 1999 at the beginning of the war, was this the establishment for anti-terrorist units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see yesterday that towards the end of 1998 the minister practically disbanded the Special Anti-terrorist Unit, that is the part of it that was based in Novi Sad, and the Special Anti-terrorist Unit practically consisted only of the unit in Belgrade and the one in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you go back to tab 32 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we call up again P357. In English it would be page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Djordjevic, page 8 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean to exhibit the last document, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I do want to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D401.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And while that is being received, the Chamber noted there appeared to be an obvious mistake on the heading of the first page of the English translation which gave the date as 1999, whereas the date in the original and at every other point in both the original and the English translation was 1996. I just mention that so that if there is any concern by counsel they will pick it up. But otherwise, the Chamber will treat it as a 1996 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, I would like that to be 1996, and we will have it corrected in English. Thank you for pointing out my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, could you look at Article 10 of the rules on internal organisation and tell us a little about how it was done in practice?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the powers granted under this article, chiefs of sectors and also chiefs of secretariats had the authority to form permanent or provisional staffs, commissions, Working Groups, and other bodies using MUP personnel within the sector, and these bodies would be tasked to deal with some more complex tasks, which required the engagement of more than one organisational unit and a number of personnel within the secretariat. And chiefs of sectors and chiefs of secretariats were the point staff to these bodies, issued tasks and dead-lines, stipulated what they -- what their duties were. But regardless of the fact that the chief of sector at the ministry had the power, the legal power in conformity with the general principles of management of the ministry, I, as chief of sector, would always draw up a proposal to set up such bodies that I had the right to establish, and then I would go to the minister to explain my proposal and my intentions. And the minister would then give me permission to follow my proposal as it was or with certain amendments he would suggest, and then only would I establish this group or staff. As chief of sector, I was able to order a chief of a secretariat to set up groups or commissions to deal with certain issues, and he would follow my orders to execute such assignments under Article 10. Therefore, as chief of sector, I was not able to form a single commission without first informing the minister and getting approval from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you perhaps tell us about the history of the establishment of staffs in Kosovo and Metohija, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security situation in Kosovo and Metohija was for a long time very complex. There were periods of extreme complexity in the security situation. But in 1981, there were large-scale protests and our priority security task was to deal with them. At that time the federal Ministry of the Interior, pursuant to a decision by the presidency established a joint police detachment which was tasked to restore law and order that had been largely disrupted by these destructive protests. The staff of this detachment was made up of commanding officers from the Secretariat of the Interior and each republic and also the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina had the duty to follow the approved plan and send a part of its forces to Kosovo. If I remember well, from all of Yugoslavia around 3.000 policemen were sent to Kosovo and Metohija. All this personnel was under the command of the staff of this joint body. They made plans and decided where and how to intervene. This staff of the joint detachment under the command of the federal Secretariat for the Interior was in operation until 1989, I believe with this particular composition and structure. In 1989, I was appointed commander of that joint police detachment. And while I was in that position, the whole situation in Yugoslavia was destabilised, and during my tenure, first the police units from Slovenia and then Croatia stepped out of this joint force and the last ones to remain were Macedonians. When they too left and when amendments were passed to the constitution in Serbia and a new state was formed called the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, this staff continued but then consisted only of personnel from Serbia and Montenegro. Later on the Montenegrins drew down as well, and the staffs then continued to consist only from personnel from Serbia and Vojvodina. After this joint force fell apart, it was renamed several times, but it continued to exist until 1999 executing whatever tasks were given by the ministry, that is the minister. We must note here that before all these changes occurred, there was a provincial Secretariat for Internal Affairs, and after these changes the provincial secretary who was an Albanian, and ethnic Albanian left that position and a greatest number of members from the base of that provincial secretariat also left the force, and then the ministry had to compensate for the disappearance of the provincial secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, when you made decisions to form these staffs, which lines of work, or rather, personnel from which sectors would be appointed to the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were made up only of members of the public security sector because their job fell within public security affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I call up 65 ter P4479. Perhaps Mr. Stamp could help us. I don't know if it was listed as a bar table exhibit from the Prosecution. I don't know if it received a number or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's number 37, Mr. Djordjevic. Your tab 37. This is your decision of the 11th of June, 1997. Could you comment briefly. This is not the right document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 10 of these rules, on the 5th of April, 1996, I passed he decision to establish a staff of the Ministry of the Interior for Kosovo and Metohija based in Pristina. In item 2 we see that the job of the staff is to plan and undertake steps and activities, and then the activities are listed. Basically the first task is to suppress armed insurgency, the second task is to prevent civil unrest, the third task was to prevent terrorism and some other complex assignments that needed to be done in the area of Kosovo and Metohija. The obligation of the staff under this decision was also to render specialised assistance to the Secretariats of the Interior, to issue orders to them, to control the execution of tasks, and by such a way of organising and setting of this staff, a step was made, so to speak, whereby I had translated delegates and certain authority to that staff and made them responsible for these most complex duties. Another of the tasks was also to be responsible for the work of the secretariat whenever complex duties needed to be carried out. In carrying out such complex work, the secretariats irrespective of such complex duties were subordinated to the staff, to the staff set up in this way. In view of such obligations, the staff, the chief of the staff, was directly responsible to me for the execution of these tasks, and he reported to me in respect of everything, specifically in respect of the tasks which are referred to in items 2 and 3 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D402.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask Mr. Stamp to check 65 ter 4271, whether that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, it is tab 38 in your binder. No, it is not. Mr. Djordjevic, please explain to us this decision of the 12th of June 1997 designating the composition of the staff. Can you explain the details for us. It is tab 38.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The previous decision was the decision setting up this institution, i.e., staff. This following decision, which we now have on the screen, is a decision on the staffing of the staff, the personnel composition of it, designating the staff leader, the staff chief, and the members by name, listed by name. That is the essence. That is the main reason why this decision was brought, to assign these people to their respective duties within the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There were seven members, as we can see, of the staff. How do you arrive at this specific staff structure and these lines of works being represented on it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular point in time, the security situation in the area of Kosovo was quite complicated. It was not that complex in fact, so that the number of members within the staff and the specific responsibilities within the staff were both reduced. That is why it features a smaller number of members because account was always taken when such decisions were being adopted, namely when staffs were being set up and the extent of the staff and the personnel numbers, account was always taken of the current situation and the tasks that the staff would have to perform at the specific time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a decision made by the present witness? Can that be made clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he has said in his response that this is actually the personnel composition as a follow-up to the previous document by which of the staff had been set up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this was my decision, but as I just said, I also prepared a proposal of this personnel scheme for the staff. I presented it to the minister, and he fully agreed that we should have such a personnel structure, and he primarily agreed to the appointment of the staff leader. I could never make my own decision to that effect and appoint anybody as staff leader without a decision to that effect having been brought by the minister. Even though according to the rules, I had the powers to bring such a decision, but I have already explained the reasons why this was done in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell us please, according to this decision who was the staff leader? Where had he worked prior to that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment the leader of the staff was Aco Vesovic, assistant chief of the administration for the traffic police of the headquarters of the ministry who, shall I say, was not widely educated in terms of interventions in mass demonstrations, large-scale riots or similar incidents so that under 2 and 3 appointed as his assistants were people who had completed the military academy and had experience in dealing with such problems in work, leadership work, and had the necessary experience in work with special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D403.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now please see Exhibit 4480 under the 65 ter list. That is the Prosecution's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your tab it is number 39. Mr. Djordjevic, this is a decision of the 15th of January, 1998, defining the duties and tasks of the staff in Pristina. Can you tell us how this document came about and why?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision in a way spells out in more detail the activities of the staff, defines the obligations of the staff, and more precisely, and the staff's tasks to co-ordinate, direct and bring into accord the work of all the secretariats in the area of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo. Practically this is expanding in some respects of the obligations that are contained in the basic original decision in its Article 2. The staff's task has also been expended to the effect that in carrying out its work, it should fully co-operate also with the state security department, with the Yugoslav army, with other state organs and local self-government organs, which was not in the previous decision because the situation that had obtained in early 1998 had started to drastically deteriorate, and there were some other manifestations of activities to which -- which were pointed out by this decision also, and which the staff had to respond more adequately to, also by drawing on all these other factors. Also through the system of co-operation and mutual exchange of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The tasks listed under 1, are they all within the public security department's ambit?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all these are tasks which are in keeping with the law where the obligation of the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you issue tasks to members of the state security department? Could you give them assignments?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not issue orders to the state security department. I only could direct staffs or secretariats formed in this way to co-operate, to exchange information on the specific security events or incidents, but I could issue orders to my staff [Real-time translation read in error "to myself"] but to state security department staff or to the organisatory [as interpreted] units, I could not, I was not so authorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I don't know whether to ask for this exhibit to be admitted or to wait for the bar table because this has been envisaged for the bar table. I'm seeking your guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Strike while the opportunity presents, Mr. Djurdjic. Tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I ask for it to be admitted into evidence. I can see that colleague Stamp is not all too enthusiastic about my proposal, but whether it's a P or a D, as long as it's in the file, it makes no difference. I believe he would probably be using it in the cross, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Received as a D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D404.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now they are telling me line 13, page 17, it should say, I could issue orders to my units, not to myself. Please correct that. Can we please now see P704. Exhibit P704.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is tab 40 in your binder, Mr. Djordjevic, which is a letter by you, I believe.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a letter dated the 23rd of January, 1998. In view of the adverse development of the security situation, I again issued instructions to the staff as well as to the Secretariats of the Interior in the area of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija with the basic tasks also referred to in the previous decisions, but what is specific about this letter is contained on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please wait for all this to also appear on the screen so that it can be followed by the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in view of the negative development of the security situation, according to this letter, the staff was also charged with the obligation of training organisational units to intervene, to act in the execution of special security tasks. And then it goes on to list the training of which secretariats, of which units, and also that the staff with its capacities should contribute to equipping all these factors, all these structures for future security tasks to be able to discharge them. Thus what is specific is that additional training is being ordered, and the organisation of such training courses in Kosovo and Metohija, in the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see Exhibit D100 which is tab 41 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But please, when we move on -- when you move to the second page, please pause for a minute so that we could have it brought up on the screen so that everybody can see it while you speak. Mr. Djordjevic, now, this is a decision of the 15th of May, 1998, signed by you. It is also a decision on the formation of a staff.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same principle as previously. On the 15th of May, I brought a decision to set up this staff in Pristina with similar mandate as those in the previous decisions, although the security situation, one could say continued to develop in a negative direction and we were confronted with serious security challenges. But in agreement with the minister, this decision whereunder this staff was formed was practically adopted in the same manner as before. Now, why was it adopted on the 15th of May, 1998? Because as a rule, these staffs in the personnel sense were set up for a year and assigned for a period of a year since the term of the previous staff was about to expire, it was to be replaced in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have a look at exhibit -- yes, yes, it is an exhibit. P760.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 42 in your binder, Mr. Djordjevic. It is a decision dated the 11th of June, 1998, on the composition of the staff.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a decision concerning the appointment of the members of the staff and the leader of the staff. We had a previous decision or previous decisions, rather, that involved seven or eight members on the staff, whereas this decision involves 14 or 15. In agreement with the minister and in view of the security situation at that point in time, we agreed to establish a staff involving this personnel. That is to say headed by Sreten Lukic, then his deputy would be Djinovic, and then there were the other members of the staff, not to go into all the names. So from that moment onwards when this staff was established, duties were taken over from the previous leader of the staff in Pristina and the new members of the staff familiarised themselves with the preparations and tasks involved practically taking over from the previous staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this decision -- actually, were all these persons personnel from the RJB?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of these are members of the public security, and the chiefs of the secretariats and the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija are also members of the broader composition of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I would like to ask for P57, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, in your binder it is tab 43. This is a decision dated the 16th of June, 1998. It is a document of minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and it has to do with the establishment of the ministry staff for combatting terrorism. What do you know about the bringing of this decision and its realisation?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation in the territory of Kosova-Metohija irrespective of various activities that had been underway because in the meantime parts of the province had been blocked and there were special activities of Special Forces and special staffs, and these tasks had been carried out but regardless of the fact that traffic was established on the roads where traffic had previously been stopped by the terrorist groups, the overall situation in Kosovo and Metohija, according to various estimates, was moving towards becoming an even more complex one. The minister's assessment was that a staff consisting of the members that we referred to just a few moments ago would not be sufficient to successfully respond to the obligations that the Ministry of the Interior had in resolving very serious security-related tasks and problems. In accordance with these assessments of his, he made a decision to establish one staff of the ministry, and that this staff should involve the RJB and the SDB, and in this way, it would involve both departments. So that in view of the fact that there was terrorism on the ground, both services had to be active in order to complete the work that lay ahead of them. On the basis of this right of his, and in view of the security assessment of developments on the ground, he decided to appoint Major-General Sreten Lukic as head of this staff. David Gajic was to be his deputy. At that point in time and for years before that, he had been in Kosovo, and he was co-ordinator for the state security there. In addition to public security personnel, the staff was to include members of the state security too. Also, as we can see on page 2 of the document -- could we please have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at the second page. Could you please wait a moment. [In English] Please second page. This is third page on the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The English has only two pages, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, could we please go back to page 1 then. Thank you. I have something for the transcript, page 21, line 23. It shouldn't just say major, it should say major general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in addition to these individual members of the staff the minister appointed in terms of the wider composition the staff, the chiefs of the centres of state security from the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosova-Metohija. On the basis of my previous decision, only the chiefs of SUP as part of the public security were members of the wider composition of the staff. Whereas in this decision, the minister fully brings together both services and gives them the task of combatting terrorism in the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosova-Metohija. That is the basic and almost exclusive task of this staff. That is to say, combatting terrorism and fully bringing together all the capacities of both services. That is to say, the state security and the public security departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you something else now. In terms of lines of work, or rather not lines of work, in relation to tasks carried out by assistants in these different sectors, is there any difference in relation to the previous decisions that you had made?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the situation that was to be expected, the staff involved the commanders of the special units of the RJB and the SDB such as Zivko Trajkovic, the commander of the Special Anti-terrorist Unit of the RJB; and Milorad Lukovic, commander of the unit for special operations of the RDB, the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you explain Roman numeral II to us now, paragraph 2, in addition to this basic task that we see here, and that is combatting terrorism?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman numeral II means that the staff plans, organises, and controls the work and engagement of organisational units of the ministry and also of sent and attached units in suppressing terrorism in the AP of Kosovo and Metohija. That is to say, it is the duty of the staff to involve all capacities of the Ministry of the Interior. That is to say, the state security and the public security, to bring them together within the same plan under the same leadership, and in terms of the same engagement in carrying out anti-terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about this second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the basic task is, what I mentioned a few moments ago from paragraph 1, under Roman numeral II, that is. And in addition to that, the staff had the duty to plan, organise, and direct and co-ordinate the work of organisational units of the ministry in Kosova-Metohija in carrying out more complex special security operations. So the difference between the first paragraph and this second paragraph lies in the following: In anti-terrorist activities, the staff should plan, organise, and control in the sense of leadership. Whereas in the case of these other tasks, there is a lesser degree of obligation. They plan, organise, and direct and co-ordinate the work of units. Since these are security related tasks of lesser importance, the staff is there as a body that directs or channels the work of organisational units of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, what are these more complex special security tasks?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These can be duties and tasks from the domain of work of public security first and foremost, and they have to do, for instance, with drug trafficking, arms smuggling, and other complex operations where the participation of two or more secretariats was required. If a particular development was taking place in the territory of two or more secretariats, then the staff was there to co-ordinate the activity among two or more secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, the head of the staff that was established on the 16th of June, was he responsible to you for the work of the staff? Did he report to you about the work of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a very clear obligation on the basis of Roman numeral III, where it say that is for his own work and for the work of staff and the state of security, the head of the staff is responsible to the minister, reports to the minister, and reports to him about security-related incidents, measures taken, and the result of such measures. In this way, through this kind of organisation of the staff and this kind of responsibility, in view of the fact that this activity of the staff involves both services, the minister of the interior, as for this particular work and planning and organising anti-terrorist activities, he practically is vesting these powers in the staff, taking them away from public security and state security. And in this way he links it directly to himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Regardless of such solutions that we have seen just now that you referred to just now, what was the situation like in terms of your previous solutions?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see that on the page where we see the minister's signature. In paragraph 6 he says that as this decision enters into force, practically all previous decisions of mine become null and void, decisions made in the previous period in 1998 and before that. So he is basically annulling all previous decisions and all decisions previously made by the chief of the RJB become null and void. That's to say they are non-existent from that moment onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in terms of equipping units, providing them with weapons, what was the situation like in that respect? Units that were in Kosovo or that had been sent to Kosovo, the secretariats as well.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The obligations were the same as previously. However, all units sent and attached to the staff from the RJB were being sent by the appropriate police administration in the RJB. As for the state security, it was the appropriate services from within the state security. Also with regard to the personal rights enjoyed by members of the staff that came from public security, most often on the basis of this decision, I would pass decisions regulating their rights derived from employment. They have to do with their salaries and their general income and other relevant matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up D99.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's your tab 44.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I forgot to say in the previous decision the minister had taken appointing members of the staff. It is said that at the request of the staff, other personnel of the Ministry of the Interior can also be sent to perform certain work at the staff. What I mean to say is that this is not -- these decisions and appointments are not engraved in stone. Other personnel can also be included, and therefore, on the 2nd of October, 1998, the minister points to the staff also Major-General Momcilo Stojanovic, assistant chief of the public security sector and gives him specific tasks that were not directly linked with anti-terrorist activities, the decision specifies his tasks. It's mainly logistics and providing the prerequisites for the work of organisational units of the MUP, construction of certain installations, or housing for employees of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I believe it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. We'll take the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you one question about this decision of the minister dated 16th June 1998. After this decision, did the staff for the prevention of terrorism of the MUP report to you as chief of sector about their work?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All duties of the staff were subject to reporting to the minister. They were answerable to the minister for everything, including reporting, therefore, the staff never reported to me about their work. I did not receive such information from them. Let me just add about this decision, I don't think we finished with it before the break concerning Momcilo Stojanovic and his appointment to the staff. Pursuant to the minister's decision, that staff could have new personnel appointed to it, additional personnel, such as in the case of Momcilo Stojanovic. But as I, as chief of the public security sector, did not have the powers to send to the staff or appoint to the staff any other member of the MUP except those approved by the minister. Everything concerning the staff was within the purview of the minister. It was up to him to decide on the personnel and make every other decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up P1044.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your binder it's tab 45.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision I signed after I returned from Kosovo. And like with any other decision addressed to staff members, it concerns only their rights and entitlements arising from employment. Therefore, under this decision the salary of Momcilo Stojanovic was increased, and he enjoyed all the other benefits enjoyed by any other member of the staff. I could make this decision only pursuant to the decision on appointment made by the minister. All the other decisions concerning rights and benefits I signed myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This decision that we are looking at now, did you make it based on your inherent powers?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could make these decisions only on the authority of the minister. That is clearly stated in the preamble of this decision and any other decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You just told us that you made this decision concerning legal and employment rights pursuant to the minister's decision. And yesterday you told us that you made certain decisions on the termination of secondment for some members of the staff. Was that also one of the powers that you had in your position?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made those decisions also on the authority of the minister because prior to that, the minister decided to appointment a certain person to a certain position and to terminate the person who occupied that position before. If that position was chief of the secretariat, for instance, I would make that decision pursuant to the minister's decision. My decisions, therefore, followed only upon the minister's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P259.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's your tab 46. Just take it easy, please, we need to have it on the screen first. Mr. Djordjevic, we see here the minister's decision dated 21 May 1999. Could you give us your comments.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of May, 1999, the minister decided to appoint Dragan Bozovic, deputy chief of the MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism, made him responsible and answerable to the chief of the staff for the tasks that he had issued him with. And any decision related to the minister's prior decisions were submitted to the leader of the staff concerned and the office of the minister. Thus, none of these decisions were submitted to the leaders of any of either service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you make a proposal to the minister to second Mr. Bozovic to be deputy chief of the MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it was not up to me to decide on the staffing of the staff. The staff talked directly to the minister and then the minister would make a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D010-0603. For the Prosecution. It's 1785. That's the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And it's your tab 47, Mr. Djordjevic. As far as I can see, this is your decision dated 21 May 1999 to appoint Dragan Bozovic to execute security tasks in the territory of Kosovo. Could you explain what preceded this decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same with prior decisions. It followed the minister's decision, and it was made on his authority to regulate certain rights and benefits arising from employment such as salary and other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is there anything the Chamber wants to ask? If not, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The problem is we query whether the document on the screen is the one that you and the witness are talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we would need the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are quite right. What we see on the screens now, that was P259. And I asked for D010-0603. Is the English version correct? No. No, this is the decision of Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think there is an error in the -- in uploading to e-court. I think the decision he wants to refer to is at page 3 -- 2 and 3 of D010-0605, so they combine the two documents in this one. I think the first page of what is before the Court should be severed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to my learned friend, Mr. Stamp. Thank you, Your Honours. This is the document that we have discussed, which is the decision of the accused dated the 21st of May, 1999. The date is the same, also the 21st of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it's not Exhibit P259. You wish now to tender this as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just need to clarify something, yes. As exhibit -- unless it was already admitted, and I'm not sure about this, I think that Mr. Stamp told me that P259 contains both documents. If that is not the case, then I ask that this document D010-0603 in the Serbian version and -05 in the English version be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D405.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to call 65 ter OTP document 4101.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 48, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And again, I would like to ask Mr. Stamp to help me and say whether this document is included in the bar table motion by the OTP. We can use it if it has already been admitted. 4101 is the OTP 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, did you receive this document? I think this is a document and not a dispatch dated the 28th of May, 1999, from the MUP staff for suppression of terrorism in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I received this document. If I did, then I was not competent to act pursuant to this document, and I forwarded this document to the person who was responsible, who was competent, which was the minister. This means that if I indeed received this, then I simply forwarded it to the minister. This document is a bit unclear to me, precisely when it comes to appointing Dragan Bozovic, deputy head of the staff, because in the earlier document we saw that on the 21st of May, 1999, pursuant to the decision of the minister, he had already been appointed deputy head or leader of the staff. Whereas in this document, we see that chief of the RJB is being sent a proposal for Dragan Bozovic to be appointed deputy leader of the staff even though this had already been completed and finalised two weeks prior to that pursuant to the minister's order. But in any rate, I did not act pursuant to this document. My duty was to forward this to the minister, and following this the minister adopted appropriate enactments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the purposes of the record, who was the person authorised to make a decision pursuant to this document?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only person authorised and competent to do so was the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Who signed this document? We don't see that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has a signature that reads S. Lukic. Do you see the second page of the English version. I think that you can see that Sreten Lukic signed it. We didn't turn to the other page in any of the versions. I think you can see it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D406.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood the interpreters, I think, Your Honours, you did not have your microphone on, and I don't know whether this was recorded in the transcript. Now, could we have P67, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your binder, that's tab 49, Mr. Djordjevic. Just take it easy, we need to see the document in both versions. Mr. Djordjevic, this is a decision dated the 31st of May, 1999, on establishment of the staff of the ministry for the suppression of terrorism, and if we turn to the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the third page right away, please, and that's the second page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So if we turn to this page, we'll see that this document was signed by Vlajko Stojiljkovic. Could you comment on this decision of the minister, please.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier we have said that as a rule the staff had existed for about a year in this composition, and that after that year passed a new decision was supposed to be adopted specifying the new composition of the staff. One year after the first decision, which was sometime in mid-June, you can see here on the 31st of May, 1999, the minister adopted a new decision on establishing the staff of the ministry for the suppression of terrorism, he designated the head of the staff and its members as well as other duties and tasks which are specified on subsequent pages but which are identical to the ones listed in the decision from June of the previous year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, apart from the personnel changes in this decision, are all other points regulated in the same way as in the previous decision from the 16th of June of the year before that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, while we are on the first page let me give a few comments about the composition. The minister fully abided by the proposal that we saw earlier which he had received from the head of the staff when it comes to personnel who was to be on this staff, members of the staff. And then on the second page of the document, the tasks and duties of the staff remain the same. The head of the staff has the same responsibility vis-a-vis the minister, so the duties and obligations from the previous decision were copied in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted now to turn to the decisions on appointments from June of 1998 that we saw earlier, your decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could go back to tab 42, which is P760.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I would like us to compare this decision of yours with the decision on appointment issued by the minister, so that's your tab 42 and 43. In your decision, Sreten Lukic was appointed head of the staff, a leader of the staff. Was this identical in the minister's decision too?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Now so as not to lose too much time, in your decision under item 4 we see Major Zarko Brakovic who was to be assistant head of staff for police affairs. Is he mentioned in the minister's decision of the 16th of June, Mr. Zarko Brakovic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then under item 6 of your decision, we see Mr. Miodrag Rsumovic, which in your decision was appointed assistant for financial crimes, white-collar crimes. Is he mentioned in the minister's decision as a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Under item 10, we see Milos Deretic, who was supposed to be assistant head of staff for wire communications. Is he mentioned in the minister's decision? Is he appointed in that decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this decision he is appointed as a member of the staff as head of communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the decision of the minister. And in my decision, he was an expert for communications in charge of communication systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where do you see Milos Deretic in the decision of 16th of June?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which decision are you reading? Your decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question is, do you see that gentleman's name in the minister's decision, which is under tab 44, the minister's decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Minister's decision of what date?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 16th of June 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is tab 43 in my binder. There is no mention of Milos Deretic here in the minister's document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Stamp, I'm comparing the decision of the head of the department of the 11th of June and the minister's decision of the 16th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, in your decision of the 11th of June under item 12 we see Gojko Celebic. Do you also see the gentleman's name in the minister's decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Djordjevic, could we turn to the 16th of June decision. We see that David Gajic is appointed deputy head of staff. In your decision of 11th of June, is David Gajic listed as a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because he comes from a different department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The third name from the top we see assistant head of staff for special operations Milorad Lukovic. Is he listed in your decision as a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He works for the state security, and I had no power to appoint him member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then underneath Mr. Lukovic, we see assistant head of staff for special anti-terrorist units, Lieutenant-Colonel Zivko Trajkovic. Is Mr. Trajkovic mentioned in your decision as a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D232, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we have before us the instruction on information and reporting of the Ministry of the Interior. Could you please give us brief explanations on this instruction and how it was implemented?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we have mentioned earlier, the minister of the interior adopted internal enactments regulating the work within the Ministry of the Interior. This instruction is one such enactment. The instruction regulates the issue of information and reporting within the Ministry of the Interior. It deals, or rather, it describes what urgent information is, daily regular providing information, monthly reporting, and annual one. And an integral part of this are security-related events concerning which information was provided. Therefore, this instruction, first of all, deals with providing information and reporting on regular routine tasks that are carried out within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now explain to us how this rule was applied in practice?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This book of rules regulates how the Ministry of the Interior deals on a daily basis with security-related information, events, and so on. Through established organisational units of the ministry, information was provided from the lowest organs and organisational units of the ministry up to the top level, the seat of the ministry, and then further on from the ministry to the units and members on the ground who were supposed to receive certain instructions on how this or that was to be done or improved. This means that if there was a security-related event which took place in the territory of a municipality and it fell within the category of events covered by this instruction, then the duty service of that municipal organ was to convey that information to the duty service of the regional organ who in turn was to convey that information to the duty operation centre at the seat of the ministry. This information is transmitted urgently by telephone at that. Of course, if that is what is envisaged. After this urgent information along the line up to the top, what follows is more detailed information about the event concerned and measures taken. Then there's more detailed information provided through dispatches and later on through daily information which was the obligation of every secretariat. They were supposed to send it to the ministry and to the duty operation centres. So with regard to such events or incidents that are reported on urgently during the day, at the end of the day full reports are compiled in detail in the territory of the secretariat about what happened in the territory of the secretariat, and then this daily survey of security-related incidents is provided to the duty operation centre. The duty operation centre in this way receives reports, daily reports, from all secretariats in the territory of Serbia. They write up a few sentences about the most important things that happened, and all these daily reports are sent to the analytics department of the ministry, that is at the seat the ministry. And then this administration after processing the matter and processing all the reports of all secretariats sends return information to all the SUPs about the most important security-related incidents that had taken place in the territory of the republic. In this way all secretariats are informed about things that happened outside their own territory, but that are important and are events that organisational units within the ministry need to know about. That is what I had to say about this urgent information and daily information. And that would be it. Regular information about certain security aspects can be periodical at the request of one of the lines of work from headquarters depending on the security subject matter involved, the administration can ask territorial Secretariats of the Interior to inform them about something additionally, and that is what they do then. In addition to these regular reports, there were monthly reports that were compiled and then the department of analytics at the seat of the ministry would compile these monthly reports on the basis of everything that had happened during the previous month. They would compile a survey consisting of a smaller number of incidents, and the users of this monthly information on the security situation in Serbia were specified, and they were provided copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In terms the subject matter involved, what was the subject of information provided on the basis of these rules, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that these were reports about regular security-related events and also some extraordinary events like natural disasters, protests of citizens, et cetera. But conditionally speaking, these are regular security-related events and incidents. All these events concerning which there was a duty to report starting from the lowest ranking organs up to the top organs was the list of such events, and then it depended on the particular subjects that were dealt with by the ministry, so it has to do with all the domains of the work, all the lines of work within the ministry. Traffic control, movement of foreigners, and so on and so forth, so there were particular fields where there was the duty to inform regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D004-2904, that is what I'd like to see now so that the Judges and the Prosecutor could see that list. D004-2904. That's the first page of the English version of that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what you told us about --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P67. That's it. I'm sorry. P67. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, how do I give you the page reference?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You have it in Serbian. That's fine. Whereas this is -- no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D232. I am sorry. It's the rules. It's the rules. The list starts on page D004-2904 of the English version. Yes, yes, right. We have it now, thank you. That's where the list starts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What are the events and incidents that need to be reported about, that's the English version. And, Mr. Djordjevic, you look at what you have, the Serbian version. So what is number 1? What is the field under number 1, and later on there's a specific reference to it as one of the subjects that need to be reported on.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that it has to do with reporting about all fields that the public security sector deals with, so the first one is crime prevention. First it's classical crime; murder, robbery, and the like. The next field after classical crime, as it were, is white-collar crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Could we have a look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead. We have it now.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: B, white-collar crimes. And then there are types of crimes listed with a specific reference to what the ministry is supposed to be informed of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the next page in English now, please. The next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, under V it says, Irrespective of the crime concerned. It says, Other events that have nothing to do with the previously listed crimes. Then the next field is public law and order, so after crime, the next line of work in the public security sector is public law and order, and then there is a specific reference to events that have to do with disruptions of public law and order, more significant disruptions, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the next page in the English version now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next field is traffic safety, and there is also the obligation to report on all traffic accidents in the territory of the secretariat and other events that have to do with safe traffic or consequences related thereto.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next field rather are border affairs, that is to say, everything that has to do with possible border incidents or events related to securing the state border. And within this line of work there is information that has to do with the stay and movement of foreigners. And incidents that occurred involving foreigners one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we have the next page of the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could we now move on?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within the same line of work in the ministry, there is a reference to passports, travel documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's clear. How about numbers 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the next field is the field of fires and explosions and other extraordinary events in relation to different kinds of disasters and also the activity of fire-fighting units. These reports involve all events and incidents in all the lines of work of public security, or rather the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have document D005-0046. From my colleagues from the Prosecution, it is 1454 according to the 65 ter list provided by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, it is your tab 51. Just a moment, please. Right, yes, we have it. Mr. Djordjevic, can you tell us what this document is. This document dated the 23rd of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch dated the 23rd of April, and the analytics department of the ministry, or rather, of the public security department is providing return information to the Secretariats of the Interior. They are actually sending a daily review of current events and occurrences relating to public security for the previous day, that is to say, the 22nd of April. I've already said that all secretariats provide the ministry with reports for the previous day, or rather, daily surveys of events and occurrences. And then on that basis, the analytics department processes all of that and then sends return information by way of a review of events that took place in the territory of all of Serbia so that all the secretariats would be informed about security-related events and incidents in respect of the previous day throughout the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D407.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document D005-0053. For my colleagues from the Prosecution, it is 65 ter number 1455 of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Djordjevic, it is tab 52. Just tell me, Mr. Djordjevic, did you receive these reports, these daily reports that we are looking at right now?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the daily reports. I received all of them. Well, not in the original sense but by way of a cross-section. At any rate, I was informed about everything.
