Also it is sent to all secretariats and the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D408.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document D005-0059. The 65 ter number is 1456.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And for you it is tab 53, Mr. Djordjevic. And then let me ask you something, Mr. Djordjevic, this report, it contains all the knowledge that the Ministry of the Interior has, in Belgrade that is, in respect of the previous day and for the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This feedback information for secretariats could only be drawn up this way. And it's based on the reports from secretariats, so if secretariats failed to include something in their report, then this administration could not take it into account and send feedback to secretariats. This administration received initial reports, analysed them, and then sent this back to secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D409.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have D005-0065. Number 65 ter 895.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What we see here is a daily overview for the 26th of April, 1999. Let me ask you, did ministry in this way provide feedback to all secretariats in the territory of Serbia concerning events?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just ask what date is it on the document which the witness is looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The report is for the 26th, and the overview is made on the 27th. You see it says, Public security related incidents and occurrences for the 26th of April, 1999. The document on the screen, that's what we are discussing, Mr. Stamp. Just a moment, Mr. Djordjevic. I don't know if it's properly translated, but the title of this document says: "Daily overview of topical occurrences and events related to public security for 26 April 1999." Can we go on, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, is the witness being shown the document which is on the screen, because now -- I thought I understood but now I see a different, now you say a different topic to the one that I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stamp, we are dealing with the same series of documents that the administration for analysis -- it just concerns a different day. On the 27 they are reporting about the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, my question was, was it in this way that the Ministry of the Interior informed Secretariats For Internal Affairs in the whole territory of Serbia about incidents and events for the previous day that were security related?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see clearly. It's addressed to Secretariats of the Interior, all, 1 through 33. They are the recipients of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D410.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now ask for D005-0075. It's 65 ter 1457.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your tab 55, Mr. Djordjevic. Just a moment, Mr. Djordjevic. This is a report from the analysis administration dated 28 April 1999 about the 27 April concerning occurrences that are interesting from the public security point of view. We see in all of these reports that they were also sent to the staff of the MUP in Pristina, to the head of the staff. Could you tell us why you also sent this report to the head of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it covers incidents and events that the staff had already been informed about, and it had even provided some of this information in the first place. And second, because of the importance of the staff. The minister wanted them kept abreast of all the security-related events and incidents in the rest of the territory of the republic. That's why they were given this feedback information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D411.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have D009-0791. 65 ter 1768.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For you, Mr. Djordjevic, tab 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last document of this kind, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The same type of document as those. Let me just ask you again --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have a translation? We do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, about the submission of these reports to the staff as well, in addition to the anti-terrorist activity that the staff was tasked with pursuant to the minister's decision, did the minister place in the staff's purview any other tasks?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before you answer, the translation is number D010-4277. We have only the Serbian. Yes, that's it. 14 May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw a moment ago in that decision that the principal task of the staff was anti-terrorist activity and tasks related to that, but in the second paragraph, the staff was also given the task to lend assistance to secretariats and to become engaged in more complex security-related events, so in this report some of such complex security-related incidents are listed, and the staff is, therefore, informed and their involvement is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D412.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P1041.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, it's your tab 57. Just wait until we get the English. This is a letter or a report from the staff dated 21 October 1998. Who is the recipient?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of October, 1998, this letter was sent from the staff to secretariats in the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija, all the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To whom at the secretariats?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the chief. It contains certain responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have page 2 in English and in Serbian. I don't think page 2 in English contains the beginning that we need. Could we go back in English to page 1 to see the beginning of this item. Yes, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Subparagraph (b) deals with what?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretariats, or rather, the chiefs of SUPs, are instructed to produce daily and urgent reports that are more precise and give more detail about the following events: First, terrorist acts. Second, police actions executed. Three, movements of the police force within Kosovo and beyond. And four, any particular interest expressed by the OSCE Mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did this information later reach you along your line of communication in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first say something about this document dated 21 October, that is after the signing of that agreement and the stipulation of various obligations of the MUP towards the mission. That document also stipulated that the MUP staff should be informed of all the things that must be reported to the OSCE verifying mission -- sorry, to the Verification Mission, the KVM, and the Ministry of the Interior received daily and urgent reports only covering item (b) 1, that is terrorist acts. Points 2, 3, and 4 on this page, the MUP staff received information from chiefs of SUPs and communicated them to the Verification Mission in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up D284.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, before we move on to this document, could you tell us whether this information under 2, 3, and 4, since you did not receive it, who did receive it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I can't recall the witness saying that he did not receive it. He was asked, Did you receive it, and he did not answer that question. And this is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That accords with my recollection as well, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I remember, Your Honour, is that the witness said that information under points 2, 3, and 4 were not received by him at the ministry. I'm asking if he knows whether anyone else received it and who. If it's leading, I'll moving on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are, and that is not my recollection of what the witness said. It may have been in your mind to follow that line, but I don't think it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My mistake, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, you said that the staff received information from the secretariats covered in items 2, 3, and 4. Did you receive information from the staff specified in items 2, 3, and 4?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said that clearly in my previous answer, but I'll repeat. Within daily and urgent reports, the Ministry of the Interior in subparagraph (b) of that previous page we saw, was only informed about terrorist acts covered in item 1. Information pertaining to 2, 3, and 4, was provided only to the MUP staff in Pristina, and the MUP staff in Pristina used it in their communication with the KVM because the MUP staff had the responsibility to inform the Verification Mission of all these events. Nobody within the ministry was informed about the movement of units and other things covered in items 2, 3, and 4. It was a very -- it was on a need-to-know basis and needed to be communicated to the KVM.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see an overview of security-related incidents, events, and information from the staff from the 14th of March, 1999, covering the period from 6.00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I just inquire, is this on the list of documents notified? I can't seem to find it anywhere. Well, I'm told it is. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's on the screen. It's already on the screen, that document. If we could only see the top of the page, it says 14 March. I think I said before, and I'm sorry if I didn't, that it's D284. And if we look at page 1 of this document we should see the date 14 March 1999. Can we see page 1. Yes, we got it in Serbian now. Can we now see the English, page 1. The number should end with 512. Is it clear now? So it's a report dated 14 March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, did you get this summary of security-related events that the staff sent to the ministry in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It lists also the topics covered in the report?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see here what events and incidents the staff reports about, reports -- informs the top leadership of the ministry. In a way this is double-track channel of informing because this summary, which the staff compiled and then dispatched to the ministry leadership was received by him from the secretariat in his area. The secretariats were under the obligation to inform the operations centre in the ministry about these same events, but in view of the fact that the staff was responsible for the security situation in Kosovo and Metohija, the staff made a sort of a cross-section, a recap of everything that had happened in this field, the most important security-related events, and sent a report to the leadership of the Ministry of the Interior. This summary of security-related -- security-relevant incidents for the previous day encompassed terrorist attacks, terrorist provocations, the number of apprehended persons, police, army, et cetera. The grave crimes perpetrated, more serious traffic accidents, fires and explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document D004-1896. For our colleagues from the Prosecution, it is 1458 according to the 65 ter Defence list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And your tab, Mr. Djordjevic, is 59. Mr. Djordjevic, this is a report of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP of the 17th of January addressed to the staff of the ministry to the head of the staff. Can you comment briefly on the topics that we see before us?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an obligation which the head of the secretariat fulfills according to the letter from the staff which we discussed a while ago dated the 21st of October, so acting upon that order and the relevant points in that order, he submits a report on the 17th of January 1999 to the staff. And it is precisely his report that in subparagraph (1) refers to terrorist attacks and provocations. Actually, it stated that there were no terrorist acts on that particular day, and in subparagraphs (2) and (3) it refers to movements of units in his area -- he refers to movements of units in his area, so that the staff might be informed of it and on its part inform the Verification Mission about it in keeping with its undertakings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does he also submit this report to somebody else apart from -- to the staff in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This letter or this patch which was forwarded, was forwarded in keeping with the previous order, and it referred to only the ministry staff. So this document reached only the ministry staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this exhibit, i.e., document be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D413.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document D004-1775, please. According to the Defence 65 ter list, it is 1774.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For you, Mr. Djordjevic, it is 59A, the tab. This is also a dispatch from the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica to the police squad. It is dated the 18th of January. Can you tell us all the addressees to whom this was addressed, this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secretariats of the Interior from the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija were under the obligation to send a daily report on security-related events at the same time to the staff of the ministry in Pristina and to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, its operations centre. Namely, everything according to the -- as according to the instructions on reporting and informing. They were to inform on all these events, and they did so inform the operation centre in Belgrade and the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I move that this exhibit be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D414.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document D004-1777. D004-1777. For the colleagues from the Prosecution, it is 1773 of the Defence 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Djordjevic, it is 65B. Just a minute until we see it on the screen. Mr. Djordjevic, here we again have a dispatch of the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica 18 January 1999, dispatch number 627. To whom was this send and what was its subject, can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an obligation that we have already referred to, namely the secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica was to inform the MUP staff in Pristina and the operation centre in Belgrade of security-related incidents and events for the previous day. Fortunately here we see that practically there had been no security-related events on the day preceding the day of the dispatch apart from the two referred to, and these events were always reported to the staff whether 15 or 2, as in this case, the staff of the ministry as well as the operation centre in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this be also admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D415.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would appear to be a convenient time, Mr. Djurdjic. We'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we see document D004-1782. According to the 65 ter Defence list, it is 1230.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in your binder, Mr. Djordjevic, it is 59C. Now, we have a daily report of the 17th of January, 1999, of the Kosovska Mitrovica police department. To whom was this addressed, Mr. Djordjevic, this report?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report dated 17th of January, 1999, was sent simultaneously to the MUP staff in Pristina and the operation centre of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, does this daily report contain planned anti-terrorist activities, and does it contain a report on executed anti-terrorist activities or on the future plans of activities of the police?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This daily report comprises the customary incidents and practices in keeping with instructions on reporting and informing. It does not contain any planned anti-terrorist activities, nor does it contain any post-mission completed activity reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D416.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see Exhibit P0157 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, it is your tab number 60. Here we have a dispatch dated the 1st of April 1999. It is a staff dispatch. To whom is it addressed? To whom is this document addressed?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the staff of the MUP in Pristina dated the 1st of April, 1999, addressed to the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija. The heads of the secretariats are instructed to inform in respect of the situation that had just developed and which concerned the campaign, the bombing by NATO forces. This dispatch made it incumbent upon the chiefs of the secretariats to inform the staff of the MUP about the bombing, the actual place, the date, the hours, and item 2, chiefs of secretariats are instructed to place special emphasis on terrorist attacks directed at MUP and Yugoslav army facilities, personnel and facilities. Under item 3 it focuses on serious crimes committed. And it also instructs the addressees to inform the staff about refugees, ethnic Albanians, and of other ethnic communities from the territory of the autonomous province.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see. Exhibit P701, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, your tab number is 61. This is a summary of security-related events incidents and intelligence recorded between 600 hours on the 24th of April and 1800 hours -- 600 hours on the 25th of April 1999, and it is by the MUP staff. To whom did the MUP staff submit these summaries, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report, or rather, a summary of security-related events and incidents which was submitted on the 25th of April from the staff -- from the ministry staff, and it relates to the events on the previous day. It is addressed to the minister, to the chief of the public security department, to the chief of the state security department, and to the chief of the analysis administration. This summary covers precisely the previously mentioned data on the air campaign by NATO forces on terrorist forces -- on terrorist attacks, and on serious crimes as referred to in the previous instructions by the staff, so according to those instructions the secretariat submitted those reports to the staff, and the MUP staff is then forwarding these to other officials and to the chiefs that I already indicated as well as to the administration for analysis. All the events which are covered in this summary report had already been conveyed to the MUP via the regular channel of information, namely the duty information services in the municipalities, in the regions, and in the operation centre on duty, duty operation centre. In other words, the staff of the ministry in this particular letter just recapitulated some of these events and informed the addressees of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did these reports contain plans for carrying out anti-terrorist activity, and do they contain reports about anti-terrorist activities that had already been carried out?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this report, there is no reference to plans of anti-terrorist action, or is there any mention of the results of such anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, from the 16th of June, 1998, when the MUP staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija was established and then throughout 1998 and 1999 until the end of the war, did you receive from the staff or from the SUPs in Kosovo reports and information about planned anti-terrorist activities, reports about activities, anti-terrorist activities that had already been carried out, or about plans concerning police activity during these anti-terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time concerned, I did not receive a single report, a single piece of information, a single plan from the staff of the MUP for combatting terrorism, which would relate to these terrorist, or rather, anti-terrorist activities, or did I receive from any of the secretariats in that area any information about where terrorists were, what the plan was in relation to them, and what the consequences were in relation to terrorists and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, during a certain part of 1998, I'm referring to the latter half of 1998, were you in Pristina while terrorist activity was planned, while the global plan was being implemented?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While you were in Pristina, did you receive written reports about that activity, or were you informed in some other way?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, as chief of the RJB, did not receive any reports about the activities of the staff either in 1998 or in 1999. However, my role in 1998 was different when compared to 1999, but I believe that will be clarified here as we move along. However, in 1998 or later, the staff did not submit any reports to me about planned activities or in terms of the activities that had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I just wanted to clarify that. I wanted to clarify what it was that you had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded this topic, but I would like to say that in relation to the previous document that we used, the transcript mentions the wrong number. It should be number 1057. The reference is wrong in the transcript. It says P0157. So the page is 55, line 20. Instead of P1057, it should say P1057. Mr. Djordjevic -- or rather, Your Honours, could we please have P66 called up. In English we'd like to have a look at page 5. Please, so in relation to the previous document, instead of 0157, it should say P1057.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I would now like to move on to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is not my page 5. It's the right document. However, in the Serbian version we would need Article 53. So let's have a look at page 3 in the English version, one page further. I need it from 49 onwards. Yes. One more page, yes, fine, excellent, excellent in Serbian. However, one page further we should look at Article 49 actually. Ah, yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since we are moving on to the question of disciplinary responsibility in the MUP, Mr. Djordjevic, we have before us the Law on the Interior, so I would appreciate it if you could tell us about the basic institutes prescribed here. How did this work in practice?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have here the decree on disciplinary responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, we are looking at your tab 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Find it, Mr. Djordjevic. Article 49.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How is this carried out in practice? Let us start with the general principles stipulated in this law.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia, Article 50 lists serious breaches of work obligations and duties. That is to say, that elements are established of serious breaches of work duties. This law in Article 52, envisages measures that can be taken. Also in Article 51, we see what the measures are for less serious infringements. For the most part, these are general measures that are elaborated later on through the decree on disciplinary proceedings. In this field, there is also a disciplinary court, and its role and duties are stated here. Also there is the appeal proceedings and in general the Law on the Interior provides for all of this, and it is later on specified in greater detail in the relevant decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1049, please. Could I have that document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic -- let us just see the document first actually. A few moments ago you mentioned to us this decree on disciplinary responsibility in the MUP. So could you tell us a bit more about this. How is this decree carried out in practice?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree regulates in detail disciplinary proceedings for minor breaches of work duty and disciplinary proceedings in case of serious breaches. There is specific reference as to what superior officers should do once they find out, about any one of these breaches, that is. And then the proceedings are dealt with before the disciplinary court, and then the higher disciplinary court until all these proceedings take place. So in cases of minor breaches and serious breaches, the immediate superior after finding out about the said breach, that is to say, if an employee from his organisational unit committed the said breach, he then interviews the responsible employee and conducts the preliminary proceedings. On that basis, he gains his own impression as to whether it's a minor breach or a serious breach. Afterwards, he makes his own proposal to the head of the organ concerned for the initiation of disciplinary proceedings. After that, the head of the organ, that is to say the chief of the secretariat or the chief of the administration concerned, initiates disciplinary proceedings by filing his own request. This is submitted to the disciplinary prosecutor, and then the disciplinary prosecutor through disciplinary proceedings presents evidence concerning the responsibility of the responsible employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Disciplinary responsibility of MUP employees is regulated in this document. What was the situation with MUP employees when crimes are committed that have to be prosecuted ex officio?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these situations action was taken, like in the case of any perpetrator of a criminal offence, an investigation is carried out, the perpetrator would be detained, and all other measures would be taken like in the case of any other perpetrator. As for his status in the organ, his superior officer can propose the measure of suspending the said person from the work organisation or the work unit until the disciplinary proceedings are completed, or criminal proceedings. But the same can be done in the case of disciplinary proceedings. At any rate, in respect of all criminal offences committed by MUP employees, this was the action that was taken. That is to say, they were treated like any other citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is one more thing that I would like to clarify. Just a moment, please, I'd like to find the relevant article, I do apologise. I've just remembered something. Mr. Djordjevic, can you explain Article 45 to us of the Law on Internal Affairs. Before criminal proceedings are completed --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, P66. [In English] page 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 45 of the Law on Internal Affairs says that an employee of the Ministry of the Interior shall have his employment terminated if a final judgement had been handed down convicting him of a criminal offence referred to in Article 34, and also his employment may be terminated if he no longer fulfills or if it is later established that he has not fulfilled any of the conditions for appointment to the state organs or the conditions laid down in Article 44. We said that the said person could be suspended until the completion of criminal proceedings. If he is convicted of criminal offences under Article 34, paragraph 1, these are crimes against the constitutional order, or other crimes. Then, according to this article, a decision is passed on the termination of his employment. There were situations when criminal proceedings would last for a very long time, and the ministry wanted practically to rid itself of the employee who committed such offences and then these proceedings can take two or three years perhaps, and then this other part, the latter part of the Article 45 is applied. So his employment is terminated that way because at that given point in time criminal proceedings were taking place against him, and that is an impediment for employment. So even before the final judgement was passed, we in this way got rid of employees who had committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify this. This is to say that this article was applied as a special institute apart from the disciplinary proceedings that could be initiated?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is a separate matter altogether. A disciplinary court can impose a measure that would imply termination of employment, so he would be laid off on the basis of such a decision of the disciplinary court. Whereas in this situation, the said person's employment can be terminated even before there is such a ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, as chief of the RJB, while you were acting chief and chief later, did you make it impossible in any way to carry out proceedings against any employee of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We in the ministry wanted the practice of the secretariat on the ground to be the same in terms of breaches of work duty. So we didn't want to have a situation when people would be treated differently in different secretariats, that is why we asked secretariats to inform us about what it is that employees had done, and they should practically ask for our approval for filing criminal reports if the said persons had committed criminal offences. This was a procedural matter. The chiefs of SUPs required that, and the proposal of the chief of the secretariat concerned would always be taken into account. That is to say, proceedings would be initiated and responsibility for policemen was never stopped or halted in any way from the ministry itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P47.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, it's 63 in your tabs. This is the decree of the 7th of April 1999, decree on Internal Affairs during a state of war. Can you tell us as of the 7th of April 1999 when this came into force, what changes were introduced by this decree, and how did it work in practice?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree envisaged some additional serious violations that can be committed by an employee of the ministry in a state of war, and it also stipulates sanctions for such violations. This decree makes disciplinary proceedings more urgent by abbreviating certain procedural actions and superiors could immediately discipline subordinates, especially for less serious violations. In view the state of war, it was the intent of the lawmaker to make disciplining easier and quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I'd like to ask you this about the decree, who made decisions under this decree? Who made decisions about serious violations of the military obligation?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the organisational unit, that is chiefs of secretariats and administrations. In addition to this decree on Internal Affairs, I believe we also sent to the secretariat some additional instructions explaining this in more detail. These supplementary instructions authorised chiefs of secretariats to make decisions in disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have D281.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's 64 in your tabs. Could you give us your comments. We see it's 9 December 1998, disciplinary report. This is before the state of war?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's typical for what I describe before. A police station in Zubin Potok is part of the secretariat for Internal Affairs of Kosovska Mitrovica. The commander of the police station in Zubin Potok sends to the head of secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica a disciplinary report against an employee of the police station Zubin Potok. This is the first step in this procedure, and after this the chief of the secretariat designates a disciplinary court, and the disciplinary court then takes over and finalises the disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D008-5248. It's 1087 on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your tab 65. Just a moment, this is 26 March 1999 when the war had already started but before the decree. Could you comment.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very peculiar situation that deserves an explanation. This is a request that the chief of SUP in Bor makes to institute disciplinary proceedings again an employee who committed a violation while he was working outside the secretariat as a member of the special police unit, because on the 29th of -- on the 20th of March, 1999, in Vucitrn, he committed a violation of his official duty. Now, what happens in such situations? Disciplinary liability was incurred at the secretariat even though the special police units were working outside the territory of the secretariat. So the duty remains with the chief of the secretariat to take action. The leader of the unit under whose command the policeman was working submits after the failed mission, a report to his chief proposing that disciplinary action be taken and that is followed up on. The commanding officer even before disciplinary proceedings are started can remove the policeman from the unit and send him back to his original secretariat if the violation was serious, accompanied by a report describing his offence, and proposed measures to be taken either in disciplinary or in criminal proceedings. This is a peculiar situation when the person is working outside the secretariat as part of another unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We are on very interesting ground now, Mr. Djordjevic. From this document we've just seen, when a decision was taken to engage an employee in a PJP unit, any disciplinary infraction that he commits as part of the PJP is subject to disciplinary action in the secretariat from which he was sent?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the specific feature of this rule. The commanding officer --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You've explained that already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D417.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Now I have a long document that I want to show to the witness, but maybe the time is running out. Perhaps it's better to do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will not then continue further today. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of December, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
